faqs.question: What does the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the genetic traits of the HIV-1 virus in your blood.

faqs.question: Why is the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test done?
faqs.answer: • To identify which antiretroviral drugs will be most effective in halting viral replication in patients living with HIV • To evaluate response to treatment for HIV • To diagnose HIV infection in infants • To monitor disease progression • To evaluate the risk of disease transmission

faqs.question: When is the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor might recommend this test if you have • a previous diagnosis of HIV, • viral load that isn’t suppressed by antiretroviral therapy, • treatment failure or drug resistance, • a high viral load even after completing treatment, or • exposure to a partner with drug-resistant HIV.

faqs.question: What if the results of the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: For a positive test, the result is “virus detected.”Abnormal results may be seen in cases if the virus uses CXCR4 instead of CCR5 as its coreceptor.

faqs.question: What to expect during the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test?
faqs.answer: A small amount of blood will be drawn from a vein in your arm and sent to the lab for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test?
faqs.answer: Avoid eating or drinking anything for eight hours before the test. Inform your doctor of any medications you are taking and of any specific requirements you have.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism test?
faqs.answer: • CD4 count: This count measures the number of CD4 cells in your blood and helps to evaluate immune system function. • Viral load test: This test measures the level of virus in your blood and helps to monitor disease progression and response to treatment.

faqs.question: What is the HIV-1 RNA Coreceptor Tropism also known as?
faqs.answer: Tropism testing or simply HIV tropism

faqs.question: What is HIV?
faqs.answer: HIV stands for human immunodeficiency virus. It is a retrovirus that attacks the immune system. Over time, it compromises the body’s ability to fight infections and diseases. HIV can cause acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS), a condition characterised by a wide array of severe symptoms due to a weakened immune response.
